page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, consisting of 4 physical cores with hyper-threading (2 threads per core). The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 8349.76 and a memory score of 2496.69. In memory bandwidth tests, it recorded 413.33 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 52.02 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, multi-core scaling shows some limitations, with Geekbench multi-core (4476.0) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (28.07 GB/sec) falling into the weak category. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with the 7B model prompt processing scoring in the poor category at 10.36 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-8 offers a high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. It is suitable for database operations, as demonstrated by its average PassMark database score of 2913.78 and a Redis SET performance of 7.13 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that fit within a 64 GB footprint.
